title: V/H/S/Mixtape
review: There's a bit too much GWAR. I'd rather have just had three high effort GWAR interludes. There are more than that here and some of them weren't good or funny enough. {V/H/S} is always worthwhile as silly Halloween tradition, like telling naff stories around the campfire. A movie to put on during your Halloween party. None of the segments were all-timers this year, but they were still better looking and more worthwhile than the majority of YouTube horror shorts. Having recently watched some older entries in the series, it's been a reminder of how much more visually distinct and fresh they have become now. I will always watch a new {V/H/S} even if they never receive much critical acclaim, as long as they stay away from heavy AI use. Looking online, it seems that every horror fan has a different opinion of them. I've seen comments saying the series fell off after {V/H/S/2}, while I think the opposite. I've seen comments saying this latest entry is the best one, and that it's the worst.
